Rashi on Pesachim 55a:10:1.english: And isn't there the night - And he could have taught [the case of] one who weeds on the night of the fourteenth [of Nisan].

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:10:2.hebrew: כב"ש - דמתניתין, דתנן: הלילה ב"ש אוסרין:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:10:2.english: In accordance with Beit Shammai - Of our Mishnah, as we learned: "At night, Beit Shammai prohibit [labor]."

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג רבינא אמר לעולם ביהודה - ודקשיא לך ליתני בארבעה עשר, ובהשרשה חד מקצת אמרינן, תרי מקצת לא אמרינן. לענין השרשה, חד "מקצת היום ככולו" אמרינן: אם היה מנכש בין השמשות של כניסת ארבעה עשר, הוה אמרינן דקלטה בי"ד שלם, ובחמשה עשר שלם, ומקצת ששה עשר; אבל תרי מקצת, כגון מנכש בי"ד, דמיבעי לן למימר תרי מקצת, לא אמרינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:11:1.english: This is the text: "Ravina said: Actually, [he is referring] to Judea" - And [as for] your difficulty — "let it teach [that one may weed] on the fourteenth" — [the Gemara answers:] "and with regard to taking root, one [application of] 'part [of the day]' we say, two [applications of] 'part [of the day]' we do not say." With regard to taking root, one [application of] "part of the day is like the entire [day]" we say: if one was weeding at twilight at the onset of the fourteenth, we would say that it took root on the full fourteenth, and on the full fifteenth, and part of the sixteenth; but two [applications of] "part [of the day]," such as one who weeds on the fourteenth [itself], where we would need to say two [applications of] "part [of the day]," we do not say.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:12:1.hebrew: שלש אומניות עושין מלאכה - בכל מקום, וטעמא מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:12:1.english: Three crafts perform labor - In every place, and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:13:1.hebrew: לצורך המועד תנן - הא דר"מ:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:13:1.english: For the purpose of the Festival we learned - this [statement] of Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:13:2.hebrew: או דילמא שלא לצורך המועד תנן - ומשום הכי אין מתחילין, אבל לצורך המועד אפילו אתחולי נמי שרי כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:13:2.english: Or perhaps [it was regarding labor] not for the purpose of the Festival [that] we learned - And for that reason we do not initiate [it], but for the purpose of the Festival, even initiating [it] is also permitted, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:14:1.english: A belt [tziltzul] - *Bendel* [Old French: a band or sash] for girding.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:1:1.hebrew: תנא קולי קולי נקט - כל הני "אין בין" חד תנא אמרינהו, וקולי קולי נקט. ברישא תנא: אין בין תשעה באב קל מיוה"כ לכתחלה אלא שזה ספיקו כו'; וסיפא תנא: אין תשעה באב קל מתענית ציבור אלא לענין מלאכה. ובחומרי דחמיר תשעה באב מתענית ציבור לא איירי הכא דתידוק מינה זה וזה שוין, ולעולם לענין רחיצה ט"ב חמיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:1:1.english: The Tanna took leniencies [after] leniencies - All of these ["There is no difference between..."] [statements] were taught by one Tanna, and he took [only] leniencies. In the first clause he taught: There is no [respect in which] the Ninth of Av is more lenient than Yom Kippur from the outset, except that this one's doubt, etc.; and [in] the latter clause he taught: The Ninth of Av is not more lenient than a communal fast except with respect to labor. And regarding the stringencies in which the Ninth of Av is more stringent than a communal fast, he did not speak here such that you could infer from it [that] this one and that one are equal; and in truth, with respect to washing, the Ninth of Av is more stringent.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:2:1.hebrew: ליטול לו את השם - כתר פרישות ויראת חטא, שאינו יכול לבטל הימנו מלכות שמים אפילו לילה אחת. לא כל הרוצה ליטלו יטלנו, דמיחזי כיוהרא ומחינן בידיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:2:1.english: To take for himself the name - The crown of abstinence and fear of sin, that he cannot set aside from himself [the yoke of] the kingdom of heaven even for one night. Not everyone who wishes to take it may take it, for it appears as presumptuousness, and we prevent him.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:3:1.english: The opinion is reversed - The Tanna who arranged them erred in one of them and reversed his opinion.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:4:1.hebrew: אמרי מלאכה לית ליה - הרואה אותו בטל, אומרים אין לו מה לעשות, ולא מיחזי כנוהג בו איסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:4:1.english: They say he has no work - [When] someone sees him idle, they say he has nothing to do, and he does not appear as one observing a prohibition on it.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:5:1.english: The night - The night of the fourteenth [of Nisan].

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:6:1.english: Initially, he taught [that it is a] custom - He made [it] dependent on custom.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:6:2.hebrew: ולבסוף תנא איסורא - דקתני בית שמאי אוסרין, דמשמע בכל מקום:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:6:2.english: And ultimately he taught a prohibition - For it teaches, "Beit Shammai prohibit [it]," which implies [that it is prohibited] in every place.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:7:1.hebrew: מה ראיה יהודה וגליל לכאן - אף כל מקום שנהגו היתר, היתר; נהגו איסור, איסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:7:1.english: What proof [are] Judea and the Galilee to here - So too, [in] every place where they were accustomed [to] permissibility, [it is] permitted; [where] they were accustomed [to] prohibition, [it is] prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:7:2.hebrew: מכלל דר' יהודה איסורא קאמר - דבני יהודה מתירין ובני גליל אוסרין. דאי מנהגא קאמר, מאי פלוגתיה דר"מ? הא ר' יהודה נמי הכי הוה אמר, בגליל היו נוהגין בו איסור שהחמירו על עצמן, וביהודה נוהגין בו היתר:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:7:2.english: By inference, Rabbi Yehuda is speaking of a prohibition - That the people of Judea permit [it] and the people of the Galilee forbid [it]. For if he were speaking of custom, what [would be] Rabbi Meir's dispute [with him]? Behold, Rabbi Yehuda also would have been saying the same thing: in the Galilee they were accustomed to treat it as forbidden, in that they were stringent upon themselves, and in Judea they were accustomed to treat it as permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:1.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold [that it is] permitted - Since he said [that] the people of Judea permit [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:2.english: One who is weeding - from among a grain crop.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:3.english: On the thirteenth of Nisan - [The Gemara] proceeds to explain why it mentioned the thirteenth.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:4.hebrew: ונעקרה בידו - השיבולת עצמה נעקרה בידו, שורשה מן הארץ, ובא לחזור ולשותלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:4.english: And [it] was uprooted in his hand - The stalk itself was uprooted in his hand, [with] its root from the ground, and he comes to replant it.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:5.hebrew: שותלה במקום הטיט - שתמהר ליקלט קודם העומר, שהעומר מתיר את הנשרשין; אבל הנשרשין אחר העומר אסורין משום חדש עד שיבא עומר הבא:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:5.english: He plants it in a muddy place - so that it will quickly take root before the omer, for the omer permits those [stalks] that have taken root [before it]; however, those that take root after the omer are forbidden on account of chadash until the next omer comes.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:6.english: The dry [ground] - [A] dry [place] that does not quickly allow [the plant] to take root.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:7.hebrew: מנכש בשלשה עשר - קתני, מנכש בארבעה עשר לא קתני. ומ"ט נקט שלשה עשר ולא קתני ארבעה עשר? אי משום דלא מיקלטה לפני העומר הקרב בששה עשר — מכדי שמעינן לרבי יהודה כו' בפ"ק דראש השנה (דף י:), ואי ארבעה עשר מותר במלאכה, נינקוט ארביסר נמי, דהא איכא מקצת ארביסר, וחמיסר כוליה, ומקצת שיתסר עד שעת הקרבתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:8:7.english: Weeding on the thirteenth - [This is what] it teaches; weeding on the fourteenth it does not teach. And what is the reason it mentioned the thirteenth and does not teach the fourteenth? If [it is] because it will not take root before the omer, which is offered on the sixteenth — now, we have heard regarding Rabbi Yehuda etc. in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (10b); and if the fourteenth is permitted for labor, let it state the fourteenth as well, for behold there is part of the fourteenth, and all of the fifteenth, and part of the sixteenth until the time of its offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 55a:9:1.hebrew: בגליל שנו - שלא היו עושין מלאכה כל עיקר בארבעה עשר, ובהן נשנית משנה זו:
Rashi on Pesachim 55a:9:1.english: In the Galilee they taught [this] - For they did not perform labor at all on the fourteenth [of Nisan], and regarding them this Mishnah was taught.

Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:14:1.hebrew: ומאי אפילו אפי' הני נמי דזוטרי - ה"מ לשנויי כדבסמוך: "אפי' הני נמי דלצורך המועד, מיגמר — אין, אתחולי — לא". אלא ניחא ליה למידחי שלא יפשוט מינה כלל, דהשתא מצי למימר דלצורך המועד אתחולי נמי מתחלינן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:14:1.english: And what is [the meaning of] "even"? Even these [items] as well, which are small - [The Gemara] could have answered, in the manner [it answers] just below: "Even these [items] as well, which are for the purpose of the Festival — completing, yes; initiating, no." Rather, it preferred to deflect [the proof] so that one would not resolve [anything] from it at all, for now one can say that for the purpose of the Festival, we may even initiate [work].

Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:1:1.hebrew: קולי קולי קתני - בלא דר' אלעזר דאסר להושיט אצבעו במים, צ"ל "קולי קולי קתני", דהא בתשעה באב לכל הפחות כל גופו אסור אפילו בצונן, ובתענית ציבור מותר בצונן, כדמוכח בפ"ק דתענית (דף יג.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:1:1.english: [The tanna] is teaching leniencies - [Even] without [the statement of] R' Elazar, who prohibits dipping one's finger in water [on the Ninth of Av], one must say "[the tanna] is teaching leniencies," for on the Ninth of Av, at the very least, [washing] one's entire body is prohibited even in cold water, whereas on a communal fast it is permitted in cold water, as is proven in the first chapter of Ta'anit (13a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:7:1.hebrew: אמר ר' מאיר מה ראייה יהודה וגליל לכאן - לרבי מאיר דאית ליה דהוי מנהגא, קסבר דלא נחלקו ב"ש וב"ה בדבר זה, דבמנהג לא שייך פלוגתא, דליחזי היכי נהוג:
Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:7:1.english: Rabbi Meir said: What proof [is there from] Judea and the Galilee to [the discussion] here? - According to Rabbi Meir, who holds that it is a custom, he maintains that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about this matter, since regarding a custom a dispute is not applicable, for let us see how they practiced.

Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:7:2.hebrew: מדקאמר ר"מ מנהגא מכלל דרבי יהודה איסורא קאמר - אמתניתין ליכא למידק הכי, מדקאמר ת"ק מנהגא מכלל דחכמים איסורא קאמרי; דאמתני' איכא למימר דתרוייהו סברי מנהגא, וה"ק חכמים לת"ק: "למה אתה סותם דבריך, והלא אתה יכול לפרש דבריך ולבאר דבגליל אין עושין וביהודה עושין?" ובברייתא לא שייך לפרש כן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:7:2.english: From [the fact] that Rabbi Meir says [it is a matter of] custom, by implication Rabbi Yehuda is speaking [of] a prohibition - Regarding our Mishnah, one cannot infer thus — [namely,] from [the fact] that the Tanna Kamma says [it is a matter of] custom, by implication the Sages are speaking [of] a prohibition; for regarding our Mishnah it is possible to say that both of them hold [it is a matter of] custom, and this is what the Sages are saying to the Tanna Kamma: "Why do you leave your words unspecified, when you could explain your words and clarify that in the Galilee they do not perform [labor] and in Judea they do perform [labor]?" Whereas in the baraita it is not applicable to explain thus.

Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:9:1.hebrew: כל הרכבה שאינה קולטת - וא"ת, א"כ למה אינו שותלה במקום הגריד? אי קלטה עד שלשה ימים — שרי לה עומר; ואי לא קלטה — שוב לא תקלוט, ואינו צריך היתר, כמו חיטי דכדא. וי"ל דבמקום הגריד מאחרת לקלוט יותר מג' ימים. א"נ, יש לחוש כשיראה שלא תקלוט, שישתול אותה במקום הטיט אחר העומר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 55a:9:1.english: Any graft that does not take hold - And if you ask: If so, why does he not plant it in a dry place? If it took root within three days, the omer permits it; and if it did not take root, it will never take root again, and it does not need permission [from the omer], like wheat in a jug. And one can answer that in a dry place it is delayed in taking root beyond three days. Alternatively, there is room for concern that when he sees that it will not take root, he will plant it in a muddy place after the omer:
